extractor: read directly from the four official Migri pages listed in source_roles
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim government wording, lowercased by the normalizer. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state.
structure_note:
ONE PAGE, TWO LEGAL REGIMES, AND THE OLDER ONE IS STILL PRINTED IN FULL. Migri publishes 'permit requirements for applications submitted before 16 june 2025' and 'permit requirements for applications submitted on or after 16 june 2025' as two complete numbered lists on the same URL. Requirements 1, 2 and the income requirement are WORD-FOR-WORD IDENTICAL between them, so those excerpts verify clean whichever block they were read from. The difference is requirement 3 of the new regime: both spouses must be at least 21. Extracting the superseded block would produce a checklist that is verbatim, provenance-complete, and no longer the law.

This is the concatenation problem from UDI's family page in a new form. There the sibling blocks were different ROUTES; here they are the same route at different TIMES, which is worse, because nothing in the wording of an individual sentence marks which regime it belongs to. So `source_bounds` runs from the on-or-after anchor to the end of the page, and verify-extraction-bounds.ts reports how many of these excerpts would also verify from outside it.

WHY THE FEE IS QUOTED FROM A DIFFERENT PAGE. The spouse page states its own fee, but that line sits ABOVE both regime blocks and therefore outside the bound. Rather than widen the bound — which would readmit the superseded regime — the fee is taken from Migri's fee schedule, which is the decree-based source anyway.

FOUR SOURCES FOR ONE PERMIT, and each carries what only it states: the route conditions (spouse page), the general entry conditions (first residence permit), the income thresholds (family income page), and the fee schedule (processing fees).

requirements.starts_at: permit requirements for applications submitted on or after 16 june 2025
requirements.note: the CURRENT regime and everything after it. The superseded 'before 16 june 2025' block sits above this anchor and is excluded; three of its numbered requirements are identical in wording to the current ones.

freshness_note: No dateModified anywhere on Migri — 'unknown', never 'fresh'. Three independent currency signals instead: the income page carries dated press releases, the most recent 20.8.2026; the fee schedule is headed 'fees of the finnish immigration service (eur) in 2026'; and the spouse page states a benefit change taking effect 1 may 2026. The income thresholds themselves are stamped 'as of 1 november 2024' by the authority, and that date is stored rather than smoothed: it is when the figures took effect, not when the page was written.
not_extracted: The superseded pre-16-June-2025 requirements. They are on the page in full and are deliberately outside the declared bound.
The worked income examples. They are arithmetic on the thresholds already stored, and copying them would duplicate figures that must change together.

The exceptions to the income requirement in general. Migri routes that question to a separate 'income requirement' page which lists who is exempt; recording 'there are exceptions' without the list would be worse than pointing at the authority.

The other family routes on this hub — cohabiting partner, spouse of a Finnish citizen, child, guardian, other relative, adoption. Each is a separate page with its own conditions and would be its own visa type.
The extended permit on the basis of family ties. A separate application.
The legalisation, translation and DNA-analysis procedures, each on its own Migri page.

requirements.label: Married to, or in a registered partnership with, the person in Finland
requirements.description: The certificate must be legalised unless it was issued in a Nordic country or an EU member state. Cohabitation is a different route with a different page.
requirements.source_excerpt: 1 you and your spouse are married or in a registered partnership. if you are married, present a marriage certificate. if you are in a registered partnership, present a certificate of registered partnership. the certificate must be legalised , unless it has been issued in the nordic countries or in an eu member state.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: 1 You and your spouse are married or in a registered partnership. If you are married, present a marriage certificate. If you are in a registered partnership, present a certificate of registered partnership. The certificate must be legalised, unless it has been issued in the Nordic countries or in an EU Member State.

requirements.label: Your spouse holds a Finnish residence permit, or you apply at the same time
requirements.description: The second limb is easy to miss and materially useful: a couple relocating together does not have to wait for one permit before the other can be applied for.
requirements.source_excerpt: 2 your spouse has a residence permit in finland or you are applying for a residence permit at the same time with your spouse.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: 2 Your spouse has a residence permit in Finland or you are applying for a residence permit at the same time with your spouse.

requirements.label: Both spouses at least 21 when the permit becomes valid
requirements.description: THE RULE THAT SEPARATES THE TWO REGIMES ON THIS PAGE, and the only numbered requirement that is not word-for-word identical to the superseded block. It is an age at VALIDITY, not at application: the application may be filed up to 9 months early, and 3 months early where the spouse holds a study permit. Joint custody of a child lifts it entirely.
requirements.source_excerpt: 3 you and your spouse are at least 21 years of age when your residence permit becomes valid. the residence permit application may be submitted at the earliest 9 months before turning 21. if you submit the application earlier, the decision may be negative. the validity period of the residence permit cannot begin before you and your spouse have turned 21. if you and your spouse have joint custody of a child, you can obtain a residence permit as the child’s parent or guardian even if you or your spouse are not yet 21 years of age. if your spouse has a residence permit for studies in finland, you can submit your application 3 months before you turn 21 or your spouse turns 21 at the earliest.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: 3 You and your spouse are at least 21 years of age when your residence permit becomes valid. The residence permit application may be submitted at the earliest 9 months before turning 21. If you submit the application earlier, the decision may be negative. The validity period of the residence permit cannot begin before you and your spouse have turned 21. If you and your spouse have joint custody of a child, you can obtain a residence permit as the child’s parent or guardian even if you or your spouse are not yet 21 years of age. If your spouse has a residence permit for studies in Finland, you can submit your application 3 months before you turn 21 or your spouse turns 21 at the earliest.

requirements.label: Meet the income requirement — and it cannot be met from the listed benefits
requirements.description: Either spouse's income counts. What does not count is named: social assistance, labour market subsidy, basic unemployment allowance, and the general social security benefit that replaces the last two from 1 May 2026.
requirements.source_excerpt: 4 income requirement. you must meet the income requirement (requirement for sufficient financial resources). you can prove that you meet the income requirement by submitting evidence of your or your spouse’s salary or income from business activities, for example. your income cannot be based on social assistance, labour market subsidy, basic unemployment allowance or general social security benefit. note that the general social security benefit paid by kela replaces labour market subsidy and basic unemployment allowance as of 1 may 2026.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: 4 Income requirement. You must meet the income requirement (requirement for sufficient financial resources). You can prove that you meet the income requirement by submitting evidence of your or your spouse’s salary or income from business activities, for example. Your income cannot be based on social assistance, labour market subsidy, basic unemployment allowance or general social security benefit. Note that the general social security benefit paid by Kela replaces labour market subsidy and basic unemployment allowance as of 1 May 2026.

requirements.label: Passport, photo, and colour copies of BOTH passports' data and annotated pages
requirements.description: Wider than the work and study routes: the sponsor's passport pages are required too, not only the applicant's.
requirements.source_excerpt: general attachments a valid passport issued by your country of nationality. for more information, see the page passports and other travel documents . show the passport when you visit a service point to prove your identity. a passport photo complying with the photo guidelines issued by the police (poliisi.fi) , or a photograph retrieval code you received from a photo shop the passport photo must be no more than 6 months old. colour copy of the passport page containing your personal data and copies of all passport pages with notes.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: General attachments A valid passport issued by your country of nationality. For more information, see the page Passports and other travel documents. Show the passport when you visit a service point to prove your identity. A passport photo complying with the photo guidelines issued by the police (poliisi.fi), or a photograph retrieval code you received from a photo shop The passport photo must be no more than 6 months old. Colour copy of the passport page containing your personal data and copies of all passport pages with notes.

requirements.label: Form LIITE_PUOLISO — completed and signed by your spouse, not by you
requirements.description: The application cannot be completed by the applicant alone. Recorded as a form in its own right because an applicant abroad has to arrange for someone in Finland to act.
requirements.source_excerpt: supplement form for spouse liite_puoliso (pdf) (your spouse or partner must fill in and sign the form).
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Supplement form for spouse LIITE_PUOLISO (pdf) (your spouse or partner must fill in and sign the form).

requirements.label: Proof you are legally in the country where you submit the application
requirements.source_excerpt: document showing that you are legally staying in the country where you submit the application.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Document showing that you are legally staying in the country where you submit the application.

requirements.label: Form MP_1 — only if you are already in Finland when you apply for a first permit
requirements.source_excerpt: form mp_1 (pdf) (if you already are in finland and apply for your first residence permit).
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Form MP_1 (pdf) (if you already are in Finland and apply for your first residence permit).

requirements.label: Documents legalised, and translated by an authorised translator if not in Finnish, Swedish or English
requirements.description: Nordic and EU-issued documents are exempt from legalisation. Some documents must additionally be verified before legalisation — a two-step process that is easy to start too late.
requirements.source_excerpt: the documents must be legalised, unless they have been issued by authorities of the nordic countries or by authorities of an eu member state. if the attachments are in a language other than finnish, swedish or english, you must have them translated by an authorised translator or by an official translator of another eu member state. in some situations, the attachments must also be verified before legalisation.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: The documents must be legalised, unless they have been issued by authorities of the Nordic countries or by authorities of an EU Member State. If the attachments are in a language other than Finnish, Swedish or English, you must have them translated by an authorised translator or by an official translator of another EU Member State. In some situations, the attachments must also be verified before legalisation.

requirements.label: Marriage or registered-partnership certificate, if issued outside Finland
requirements.description: Conditional on where the marriage took place: Migri already holds the record for one contracted in Finland.
requirements.source_excerpt: marriage certificate if the marriage was contracted in another country than finland. certificate of registered partnership if the partnership was registered in another country than finland.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Marriage certificate if the marriage was contracted in another country than Finland. Certificate of registered partnership if the partnership was registered in another country than Finland.

requirements.label: Divorce, dissolution or death certificate for any previous marriage — either spouse's
requirements.description: It applies to the sponsor's history as much as the applicant's, which is not obvious from a list written in the second person.
requirements.source_excerpt: divorce certificate (if your spouse or you have previously been married to someone and have divorced) certificate of dissolution of registered partnership (if your spouse or you have previously been in a registered partnership that has been dissolved) death certificate (if your spouse or you have previously been married or in a registered partnership and the former spouse has died).
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Divorce certificate (if your spouse or you have previously been married to someone and have divorced) Certificate of dissolution of registered partnership (if your spouse or you have previously been in a registered partnership that has been dissolved) Death certificate (if your spouse or you have previously been married or in a registered partnership and the former spouse has died).

requirements.label: Prove your identity at a Finnish mission abroad, and wait for the decision there
requirements.description: Migri states the exception narrowly: a first permit can be applied for inside Finland only in certain exceptional situations.
requirements.source_excerpt: 3 prove your identity. book an appointment to visit a finnish mission (finlandabroad.fi) to prove your identity. applications for a first residence permit can be submitted in finland only in certain exceptional situations.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: 3 Prove your identity. Book an appointment to visit a Finnish mission (finlandabroad.fi) to prove your identity. Applications for a first residence permit can be submitted in Finland only in certain exceptional situations.

requirements.label: The threshold is NET income, and it depends on where in Finland you will live
requirements.description: Net of tax and of pension and insurance contributions — so a gross salary comfortably above a threshold can still fail it. The amount varies by municipality because housing costs do.
requirements.source_excerpt: the required income is calculated from your net income, that is, from income that remains after tax and after employer’s and employee’s pension and insurance contributions. the amount of money that is required is based on the basic social assistance granted to beneficiaries of social assistance by kela and on the housing costs and healthcare expenses that are observed when granting social assistance. the amount of money that you must have depends on where you live, since there is regional variation in housing costs.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: The required income is calculated from your net income, that is, from income that remains after tax and after employer’s and employee’s pension and insurance contributions. The amount of money that is required is based on the basic social assistance granted to beneficiaries of social assistance by Kela and on the housing costs and healthcare expenses that are observed when granting social assistance. The amount of money that you must have depends on where you live, since there is regional variation in housing costs.

requirements.label: Some benefits DO count: child benefit, child care and maintenance allowance, study grant, housing allowance
requirements.description: The mirror image of the excluded benefits, and worth stating: a family reading only the exclusion list would undercount its own resources.
requirements.source_excerpt: certain social benefits reduce the amount of financial resources required. these are called ‘social security benefits compensating for expenses’. for example the following benefits belong to this category: child benefit child care allowance child maintenance allowance study grant housing allowance
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Certain social benefits reduce the amount of financial resources required. These are called ‘social security benefits compensating for expenses’. requirements.label: Migri may deviate from the sums for families with children, on request and with evidence
requirements.description: Discretionary, and only where the shortfall is slight or a child's best interest requires it. Recorded because the request has to be made and supported — it is not applied automatically.
requirements.source_excerpt: for families with children, we may deviate from the required sums on a case-by-case basis if the family’s income is slightly below the income threshold. making an exception to the income requirement is possible if there are exceptionally weighty reasons or if a derogation is in the best interest of a child. if you are requesting an exception to the income requirement, submit an explanation and documents supporting your claim.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: For families with children, we may deviate from the required sums on a case-by-case basis if the family’s income is slightly below the income threshold. Making an exception to the income requirement is possible if there are exceptionally weighty reasons or if a derogation is in the best interest of a child. If you are requesting an exception to the income requirement, submit an explanation and documents supporting your claim.
